name: Justin Wagner
bio: Justin Wagner is a Democratic candidate for Pennsylvania's 16th District from the Greenville area of Mercer County. He served in the U.S. Army, including a 2006 deployment to Iraq, and later in the Army Reserve. He has worked about 15 years as a senior automation engineer and is a former UAW and IBEW member.

platform.point: Proposes a 12-year congressional term limit, a stock trading ban for members, and overturning Citizens United; declines corporate PAC money.
Wants higher tax rates on wealthy individuals and corporations and criticizes the 2017 tax cuts.
Supports moving toward Medicare for All, Medicare drug price negotiation and defending Medicaid from cuts.
Backs the PRO Act, a higher inflation-indexed minimum wage and lifting the Social Security payroll tax cap.
Calls for an independent federal AI authority with binding standards, a national privacy law and a data center moratorium.
Wants to end masked enforcement operations, guarantee due process, protect DACA and create a path to citizenship.

economy.evidence: Supports higher taxes on the wealthy and corporations, a higher minimum wage tied to inflation, the PRO Act and a ban on hedge funds buying single-family homes.

welfare.evidence: Supports a transition to Medicare for All and expanding Social Security.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: would codify Roe and repeal the Hyde Amendment; guns: supports the individual right to bear arms alongside universal background checks and red flag laws.

security.evidence: Wants limits on corporate data harvesting, a national privacy law, and an end to masked immigration enforcement with habeas corpus guaranteed.

immigration.evidence: Supports a workable path to citizenship, DACA protections and due process in enforcement.

foreign.evidence: Requires congressional approval for military action, opposes unauthorized escalation with Iran and opposes Israeli military actions in Gaza.

energy.evidence: Calls for cutting emissions, investing in clean energy jobs and stronger Clean Air and Clean Water Act enforcement.

tech.evidence: Proposes an independent federal AI regulator with binding standards, the American Privacy Rights Act and a data center moratorium.

education.evidence: Opposes voucher programs that divert public school funding and wants Title I fully funded.

name: Chris Deluzio
bio: Chris Deluzio has represented Pennsylvania's 17th District since 2023. A Thornburg native and Naval Academy graduate, he served as a Navy officer including in Iraq, then worked as a lawyer on voting rights at the Brennan Center and at the University of Pittsburgh's cyber law institute. In Congress he has focused on rail safety after the East Palestine derailment and on labor issues.

platform.point: Has introduced bills to tighten hazardous materials rail transport rules after the East Palestine derailment.
Backs the PRO Act and worker protection bills as vice chair of the Labor Caucus.
Supports universal coverage and cosponsored the Medicare for All Act.
Cosponsored the Shrinkflation Prevention Act and highlights rising health insurance premiums.
Released a report on smartphone use in schools after months of stakeholder research.

economy.evidence: Cosponsored the PRO Act and the Shrinkflation Prevention Act and advocates protections for steelworker jobs.

welfare.evidence: Cosponsored the Medicare for All Act and supports universal health coverage.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports legal abortion and criticized the reversal of Roe v. Wade.

foreign.evidence: Backed Israel after October 7 and opposed a ban on cluster munitions for Ukraine, but in 2026 cosponsored a bill blocking offensive weapons sales to Israel.

name: Tony Guy
bio: Tony Guy is the Republican nominee for Pennsylvania's 17th District and a lifelong Beaver County resident. He spent 26 years with the Pennsylvania State Police and was elected Beaver County sheriff in 2016.

platform.point: Wants to reduce regulation, control federal spending to fight inflation, and support manufacturing, natural gas and agriculture.
Would fund and finish the border wall, reinstate Remain in Mexico and deport immigrants who commit crimes.
Supports giving police more tools and training and opposes efforts to defund police.
Pledges to protect Second Amendment rights for gun owners, hunters and sportsmen.
Supports voter ID requirements and prosecuting election law violations.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting regulatory burdens, controlling federal spending and opposing policies he describes as socialist.

liberty.evidence: Guns: pledges to protect Second Amendment rights; the campaign site states no position on abortion, drugs or LGBTQ issues.

security.evidence: Wants police equipped with more tools and training and opposes defunding police.

immigration.evidence: Would finish the border wall, reinstate Remain in Mexico and deport criminal immigrants.

energy.evidence: Supports developing regional natural gas and natural resources for energy independence.

notes: Liberty was lowered from 80 to 30 because the only cited evidence is support for gun rights, which sits on the individual-choice end of the scale.

name: Gabe Amo
bio: Gabe Amo has represented Rhode Island's 1st District since winning a 2023 special election. Raised in Pawtucket, he worked in intergovernmental affairs in the Obama and Biden White Houses, most recently as deputy director, and in Governor Gina Raimondo's office. He is a Wheaton College graduate and Marshall Scholar.

platform.point: Prioritizes strengthening retirement security, including protecting Social Security and Medicare.
Lists ending gun violence among his main priorities.
Focuses on climate change resilience for Rhode Island.
Supports securing reproductive freedom and abortion rights.
Wants to create jobs in future supply chain sectors for working families.

economy.evidence: Voted against the 2025 Republican tax and Medicaid bill.

welfare.evidence: Campaigned on protecting Social Security and Medicare and opposed the 2025 bill's Medicaid cuts.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports abortion rights; guns: prioritizes action against gun violence.

foreign.evidence: Voted for the April 2024 military aid packages for Ukraine, Israel and Taiwan.

energy.evidence: Lists climate change resilience among his priorities and has emphasized addressing climate change.

name: Kellie Keenan
current_role: Public health professional and small-business owner
bio: Kellie Keenan is the Republican nominee for Rhode Island's 1st District. Her campaign describes her as a public health professional and small-business owner.

platform.point: Wants lower costs for working families, tax relief for seniors and more affordable housing.
Aims to cut Rhode Island energy costs, increase ratepayer transparency and explore next-generation nuclear power.
Would reduce regulatory burdens and expand job-linked workforce training.
Promises to eliminate wasteful spending and crack down on fraud.
Supports school choice, education transparency and parental rights in schools.

economy.evidence: Backs tax relief and reduced regulation for small businesses and cuts to wasteful spending.

immigration.evidence: Lists border security among her priorities.

energy.evidence: Favors diversifying energy sources, including next-generation nuclear, to lower costs.

education.evidence: Supports school choice and parental rights in schools.

notes: Campaign site social icons link only to generic platform homepages, so no accounts are listed.

name: Wilfred Curioso
bio: Wilfred Curioso is an independent candidate for Rhode Island's 1st Congressional District.
notes: No campaign website, biography or issue statements were found.

name: Seth Magaziner
bio: Seth Magaziner has represented Rhode Island's 2nd District since 2023 and sits on the House Natural Resources Committee. He was Rhode Island General Treasurer from 2015 to 2023 and earlier worked in investments and as a Teach For America teacher in Louisiana. He is from Bristol, Rhode Island.

platform.point: Prioritizes protecting Social Security and Medicare.
Wants cheaper prescription drugs and to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act.
Supports enacting gun safety measures.
Pledges to defend abortion rights.
Wants a faster clean energy transition, lower energy costs and support for offshore wind such as Revolution Wind.
Cosponsored a bipartisan bill to ban stock trading by members of Congress.

economy.evidence: Voted against the 2025 Republican tax and Medicaid bill and campaigns on lowering drug and family costs.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare and to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: pledges to defend abortion rights; guns: supports gun safety measures.

energy.evidence: Says he is committed to accelerating the clean energy transition and backed resuming the Revolution Wind project.

name: Victor Mellor
bio: Vic Mellor is the Republican nominee for Rhode Island's 2nd District and a U.S. Marine Corps veteran who was born and raised in Rhode Island. He describes himself as a builder and businessman and is a founding member of the Great American Health Alliance, a health care reform group.

platform.point: Wants a system built on price transparency, lower costs, patient choice and medical freedom, including most-favored-nation drug pricing.
Aims to attract industries offering well-paid jobs and to cut energy, housing and grocery costs through deregulation.
Supports removing immigrants here illegally who commit crimes and a residency path for law-abiding, tax-paying workers.
Backs parental rights, free speech protections, Second Amendment rights and election integrity.
Require federal audits of road and bridge spending to root out waste and fraud.

economy.evidence: Favors deregulation to lower energy, housing and grocery costs.

liberty.evidence: Guns: supports Second Amendment rights; speech: backs free speech protections; also supports medical freedom.

immigration.evidence: Supports immediate removal of criminal immigrants but also a path to permanent residency for law-abiding, tax-paying foreigners.

education.evidence: Lists parental rights among his priorities.

notes: He campaigns as Vic Mellor; the ballot name is kept as Victor Mellor.

name: Armando Anzoli
bio: Armando Anzoli is an independent candidate for Rhode Island's 2nd Congressional District.
notes: No campaign website, biography or issue statements were found.

name: Jenny Costa Honeycutt
bio: Jenny Costa Honeycutt is the Republican nominee for South Carolina's 1st District and serves on the Charleston County Council. A James Island native, she is an attorney who practiced at a statewide firm before opening her own law firm focused on regulatory and business law. She holds degrees from Meredith College and the University of South Carolina School of Law.

platform.point: Pledges to stand with law enforcement and stop fentanyl trafficking and illegal immigration.
Would fight wasteful spending and work toward a balanced federal budget.
Promises to protect free speech, religious liberty and Second Amendment rights and limit government overreach.
Supports pro-life policies and keeping transgender athletes out of women's sports.
Wants to lower grocery, housing and health care costs for families.
Backs a Make America Healthy Again focus on prevention, food transparency and health agency accountability.

economy.evidence: Pledges to cut wasteful spending and work toward a balanced budget.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports pro-life policies; LGBTQ: would bar transgender athletes from women's sports; guns and speech: backs Second Amendment and free speech protections.

security.evidence: Promises to stand with law enforcement as the basis of safe communities.

immigration.evidence: Calls for a secure border and stopping illegal immigration.

faith.evidence: Lists defending religious liberty as a platform plank.

notes: Her county council seat comes from the Wikipedia election page; the campaign site does not name the office.

name: Nancy Lacore
bio: Nancy Lacore is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 1st District. She served 35 years in the U.S. Navy, starting as a helicopter pilot, and retired as a vice admiral after serving as commandant of Naval District Washington and as Chief of Navy Reserve from 2024 to 2025. She was born in Albany, New York.

platform.point: Would lower housing costs by ending tariffs on building materials, banning algorithmic rent pricing and cutting closing costs.
Wants to restore ACA subsidies, cap out-of-pocket drug costs and expand Medicare drug price negotiation.
Proposes capping child care costs at 7 percent of family income.
Supports a permanent offshore drilling ban, clean energy expansion and living shorelines.
Backs border security with accountability, including due process and body cameras for ICE agents.
Supports overturning Citizens United and banning individual stock trading by members of Congress.

economy.evidence: Supports banning algorithmic rent pricing, expanding Medicare drug negotiation, small-business tax credits and ending the Trump tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Wants restored ACA subsidies, capped drug costs and child care capped at 7 percent of family income.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: would guarantee reproductive rights in federal law.

security.evidence: Calls for ICE to follow due process and wear body cameras.

immigration.evidence: Pairs border security with enforcement accountability and a streamlined immigration system.

energy.evidence: Supports a permanent offshore drilling ban and expanded clean energy.

name: Bill Reeside
bio: Bill Reeside is the Libertarian candidate for South Carolina's 1st District. He is a nuclear engineer with more than 40 years in the power and research industries, including work on nuclear diplomacy with North Korea under Presidents Clinton and George W. Bush, and now works with Habitat for Humanity of York County. He has lived in South Carolina for nearly two decades.

platform.point: Would repeal presidential tariff powers, the Insurrection Act, the Patriot Act and all current military force authorizations.
Proposes stabilizing and personalizing Social Security and Medicare, including a higher retirement age.
Supports unlimited visa programs for high- and low-skill workers with guaranteed jobs, which he distinguishes from open borders.
Opposes funding military operations in Iran and would cut future defense budgets.
Sees nuclear power as the best source for data centers but criticizes large state tax breaks for them.

economy.evidence: Emphasizes fiscal discipline and would strip the president of tariff authority.

security.evidence: Would repeal the Patriot Act and the Insurrection Act.

immigration.evidence: Supports unlimited visa programs for high- and low-skill workers who have a job waiting, and says immigration helps fund social programs.

foreign.evidence: Would repeal all military force authorizations and cut defense budgets, opposing funding for Iran operations.
